data.title: Ablaut Reduplication Spellchecker
data.solution:
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
    phrase = gets.chomp
    separator = phrase[/[- ]/]
    words = phrase.split(separator)
    corrected_words = words.sort_by{|word| "iao".index( word[/[iao]/] ) }
    puts corrected_words * separator
end
data.statement:
In English, there are phrases like {{zig-zag}} and {{flip flop}} that repeat a similar word structure but change the first vowel.

These phrases tend to follow a hidden rule known as 'Ablaut reduplication'.

This rule says that the order of words in such phrases should be ordered by the first vowel, with the order "{{i}} < {{a}} < {{o}}" (e.g. {{tic-tac-toe}}).

Given an integer [[n]], and then [[n]] lines of [[phrases]] (separated by spaces or {{-}}), print the corrected phrases, reordering the words if necessary and using the same separator.

<<Wikipedia:>> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ablaut_reduplication

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

In English, there are phrases like zig-zag and flip flop that repeat a similar word structure but change the first vowel.

These phrases tend to follow a hidden rule known as 'Ablaut reduplication'.

This rule says that the order of words in such phrases should be ordered by the first vowel, with the order "i < a < o" (e.g. tic-tac-toe).

Given an integer n, and then n lines of phrases (separated by spaces or -), print the corrected phrases, reordering the words if necessary and using the same separator.

Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ablaut_reduplication
Input
Line 1: An integer n for the number of phrases to be corrected
Next n lines: A 2 or 3 word phrase to be corrected, separated by spaces or -
Output
n lines: The corrected phrase for each input phrase, using the same separator
Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10
phrase is all lowercase letters, plus spaces and - as word separators.
phrase is always 2 or 3 words.
All words will contain a, i, or o as their first vowel.
Example
Input
1
zag-zig
Output
zig-zag
